title: An investor writing from Gmail is not one of us

objects.subject: Kitebird deck?
objects.body:
Hi Meera,

I'm an angel investor in health tech and loved your clinic scheduling demo. Could you send your deck and a time to talk this week?

Kavita Rao

questions.text: Send the deck and a time to talk this week
questions.quote: Could you send your deck and a time to talk this week?

exchange_intent.motive: the deck and a time to talk

notes: STEP-04. Production: the founder writes from Gmail, and the support lane took the domain of orgs.email as ours, so every gmail.com sender was one of us - an investor writing from Gmail could never be answered late. Built with the founder's real identity shape.

answer.rationale: A direct question is waiting on us.
A person asked us for something; none of the support plays fits, and answering first is the closest.

answer.headline: Send Kavita Rao your deck and a time to talk
answer.situation: Kavita Rao asked 3 days ago: "Could you send your deck and a time to talk this week?"
answer.artifact: Hi Kavita, attaching our deck. Would [day, time] this week work for a call?

facts.claim: Kavita Rao wrote on the eighteenth of September that she is an angel investor in health tech and loved Kitebird's clinic scheduling demo.
facts.quote: angel investor in health tech and loved your clinic scheduling demo.

facts.claim: She asked for the deck and a time to talk this week.
facts.quote: deck and a time to talk this week?

facts.claim: Her ask is open and waits on us, and the file names the move as ours.
She writes from a personal Gmail address, not a firm's.
The brief names no kind of work for her; the engine filed her as an investor contact under fundraising.

inferences.claim: An angel who saw the demo and asked for the deck is a warm investor for the seed round, and she is waiting on us.
She named this week; the longer the deck takes, the cooler her interest.
Writing from Gmail, as the founder also does, does not make her one of us: she is a counterparty waiting on an answer.

hypotheses.proposition: Kavita invests on her own account, so a call could lead straight to a decision.
hypotheses.needs: The call itself, or her saying how she invests.

unknowns.question: Whether the founder has already answered her on another channel.
unknowns.relevance: A reply the file cannot see would make this one a duplicate.

unknowns.question: How Kavita saw the demo — at an event, through an introduction, or a recording.
unknowns.relevance: If someone introduced her, they should hear what came of it.

unknowns.question: Her usual cheque size, and whether she leads or follows.
unknowns.relevance: It decides how much of the founder's time the round can give her.

frames.primary: A warm inbound angel investor asking for the deck and a call this week; the move is ours.
rivals: A health-tech angel collecting decks across the sector, where the call is a first look rather than a decision.
Someone not yet a serious investor — the file holds only her own description.

proposed_kind.why: Kavita introduces herself as an angel investor in health tech and asks for the deck and a call, and the engine already treats her as an investor contact.

expected_vs_actual.expected: Without a playbook, her own ask sets it: the deck and a time to talk, this week.
expected_vs_actual.actual: Her mail of the eighteenth waits on us; nothing has gone back yet.

scenarios.do_nothing: The week she named passes, her interest cools, and an investor who came to you unasked is lost quietly.
scenarios.act: The deck and a time reach her while the demo is fresh, and a first call goes in the calendar.
scenarios.best: A first call leads to a cheque in the seed round.
scenarios.worst: A late answer reads as a company not raising in earnest, and she moves on.
signals_to_watch: Her answer to the deck, and a time agreed.
Questions from her after reading the deck.
Silence from her after the deck goes.

reasons: Raising the seed round is the brief's first goal, and she came to the founder unasked.
She asked for this week, and the move is ours.
Interest from a demo cools quickly; a late answer cannot be taken back.

next_move.what: Reply to Kavita with your deck and ask her to pick a time to talk.

answer.alternative: If the deck is not ready to share, reply now with an offer to talk and say the deck follows after the call.
answer.wait_or_stop: Do not wait: she asked for this week. After the deck goes, give her a few days; if nothing comes, one short note with something new, then stop.
answer.done_when: Kavita has the deck and a call with her is on the calendar.
answer.draft: Hi Kavita, thank you — I'm glad the clinic scheduling demo landed. Here is the Kitebird deck. I'd love to talk: which time suits you? I'll send an invite. Best, Meera
